items.title: Anthropic uses Claude AI to identify cryptographic weaknesses in security protocols [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic has employed its Claude AI model to discover vulnerabilities in cryptographic systems, highlighting potential security risks. This research demonstrates how advanced AI can assist in analyzing and testing cryptographic protocols for weaknesses. The findings may influence future approaches to securing digital communications and prompt further investigation into AI-assisted security analysis.

items.title: Researchers introduce Kimi Linear, a hybrid linear attention architecture that outperforms full attention across short and long contexts and reinforcement learning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Kimi Linear is a new attention architecture featuring Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), which extends Gated DeltaNet with a finer-grained gating mechanism to better utilize finite-state RNN memory. The design includes a chunkwise algorithm using specialized Diagonal-Plus-Low-Rank transition matrices to improve hardware efficiency and reduce computation compared to general DPLR formulations. The team pretrained a 3-billion activated parameter model combining KDA and Multi-Head Latent Attention, demonstrating superior performance over full MLA across various tasks while reducing key-value cache usage by up to 75% and increasing decoding throughput up to six times for a 1 million token context. The researchers have open-sourced the KDA kernel, vLLM implementations, and released pretrained and instruction-tuned model checkpoints to support further research.

items.title: Harmony Explained: A Scientific Theory of Music Derives Major Scale, Chord Dictionary, and Triad Feelings
items.content_text: This 2012 paper proposes a scientific theory of music harmony by combining physical and computational perspectives, aiming to explain fundamental musical phenomena such as the Major Scale, the Standard Chord Dictionary, and the emotional difference between Major and Minor Triads. The author critiques 19th-century physicist Hermann Helmholtz's theory on consonance and offers original derivations for chord structures and their emotional qualities. Written in an accessible style, the paper targets both scientists and musicians seeking a clearer understanding of tonal music's properties.

items.title: Essay argues banning AI will not stop its adoption due to low barriers and widespread utility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: An essay compares AI adoption to navigating ocean currents, suggesting that banning AI is ineffective because the technology is rapidly embraced across generations and cultures due to its ease of use and significant productivity gains. The author highlights that unlike past technological revolutions, AI requires minimal barriers to entry, enabling creative individuals to benefit immediately. The piece warns that resisting AI adoption is like swimming against a strong current, implying that adaptation is necessary to avoid being overwhelmed.

items.title: AE Studio seeks experienced divers to recover shipwreck treasures located by AI analyzing Spanish colonial records [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: AE Studio is using large language models to analyze around eighty million pages of historical Spanish colonial documents to identify coordinates of undiscovered shipwrecks and lost cargo. The company is recruiting skilled divers with extensive nautical experience to physically explore these AI-generated locations and recover treasures. Applicants must have proven open ocean experience, diving certifications or equivalent skills, and the ability to operate in challenging conditions and unfamiliar jurisdictions. Compensation includes equity, a base salary ranging from $50,000 to $500,000, and profit shares from recovered cargo after legal proceedings. The venture emphasizes discretion, physical capability, and a bias toward action in its salvage operations.

items.title: Apple becomes second company to reach $5 trillion valuation as investors retreat from AI and semiconductor stocks amid tech sell-off [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Apple has reached a $5 trillion market capitalization, becoming only the second company to do so after Nvidia. This milestone comes as investors pull back from AI and semiconductor stocks amid concerns over high capital spending and competition, leading to a broader tech market sell-off. Apple's strong product demand and decision to avoid heavy AI infrastructure investments have helped it outperform peers during this period. The company also recently launched a device leasing program in the US to support demand. Apple is expected to report a significant revenue increase in its upcoming quarterly earnings.

items.title: Manim animation engine used by 3Blue1Brown now runs in browsers via WebGPU
items.content_text: A web-based version of Manim, the animation engine behind 3Blue1Brown's videos, has been developed to run directly in browsers using WebGPU technology. This enables users to create and view mathematical animations without installing software locally.

items.title: OpenAI reports on scientists using AI coding agents to accelerate and modernize scientific software development in genomics and other data-rich fields [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A field report from OpenAI details how researchers are employing AI coding agents to improve scientific computing, enabling faster software development and maintenance in genomics and related disciplines. These agents help reduce engineering constraints, allowing scientists to focus more on directing research rather than implementation. The report covers eight projects using Codex and Claude Code agents, highlighting improvements such as modernizing legacy codebases and optimizing workflows. While agents speed up initial development, human oversight remains crucial for validating scientific accuracy and managing complex edge cases. The findings suggest AI agents can expand research capabilities but long-term stewardship and expert judgment are still essential.

items.title: Over 1,100 employees from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta petition US government to regulate AI development and support international governance efforts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: More than 1,100 workers from leading AI companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have signed a petition urging the US government to help deliberately pace AI development and back international efforts to create technical and governance tools. The petition highlights concerns about the risks of AI systems that may be difficult to understand or control. The petition reflects growing unease among AI employees about the rapid technological arms race and its consequences, including environmental impact, copyright issues, and employment disruption. However, some observers question the timing and effectiveness of seeking government intervention after significant investments have been made and amid a federal government perceived as inconsistent in its AI regulatory approach and international cooperation.

items.title: Report: Google withdrew from the AI race, with DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis betting on world models over recursive self-improvement approaches favored by OpenAI and Anthropic [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Google's apparent retreat from the AI race is attributed to a strategic decision led by DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, who favors developing world models that simulate real-world understanding rather than pursuing recursive self-improvement methods championed by startups like OpenAI and Anthropic. This shift reflects a fundamental divergence in AI research philosophy and places Google in a high-stakes position to either lead or fall behind in future AI advancements. While OpenAI and Anthropic rapidly advance AI through autonomous coding agents and large-scale compute, Google is investing in alternative approaches that may take longer but aim for more comprehensive artificial general intelligence. Despite public appearances of competition, insiders suggest Google has effectively withdrawn from the current AI race to focus on this different path, leveraging its existing business to sustain long-term AI research efforts. This strategic divergence highlights a broader contest between startup-driven rapid innovation and incumbent-backed foundational research, with significant implications for the future direction of AI development and industry leadership.

items.title: TSMC commits an additional $100 billion to expand Arizona chip factory capacity amid multi-year AI demand surge [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: TSMC is accelerating the build-out of its Arizona semiconductor factory by investing an additional $100 billion, raising its total U.S. investment to $265 billion to meet growing multi-year demand driven by AI applications. The company plans to convert more capacity to advanced 3-nanometer and 2-nanometer technologies, which are expected to drive revenue growth in the coming quarters. TSMC's CFO Wendell Huang cited strong customer demand and government support as key factors behind the expansion, despite higher U.S. construction costs compared to Taiwan. The company also continues to comply with export controls while serving Chinese customers, who account for about 8% of revenue. TSMC is focusing on both front-end wafer fabs and back-end advanced packaging fabs to foster the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem and support long-term growth in specialty technologies such as image sensors through joint ventures.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic endorse letter urging US government to support international effort to pace AI development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

The letter reflects growing industry concern about managing the rapid development of AI technologies and calls for coordinated global action to ensure responsible progress.

items.title: Jump Capital raises $350 million fund to expand AI startup investments, matching its 2021 fund size [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Jump Capital, a Chicago-based venture capital firm backed by the founders of Jump Trading, has raised a new $350 million fund to increase its investments in AI startups, co-founder Sach Chitnis said. This fund matches the size of its previous 2021 vehicle, which focused heavily on crypto before the firm spun off its crypto team into Jump Crypto. Despite the crypto market downturn, Jump Capital's portfolio company BitGo went public this year with a $2 billion valuation.

items.title: Magpie launches CLI tool to enable AI agents to perform bookkeeping with encrypted, auditable double-entry accounting [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Magpie is a command-line interface designed to help small teams and AI agents manage bookkeeping tasks securely without direct database access. It supports chart-of-accounts management, double-entry journals, invoices, payouts, and audit reads, enforcing role-based access control and accounting invariants before recording encrypted, immutable events. The tool requires Go 1.26.5 or later and can be used locally or with a hosted Jaybase backend for production. Magpie is pre-1.0 but includes features like AES-256-GCM encryption, bearer-authenticated access, and workflows for customers and invoices. It is not a full accounting SaaS and excludes features like bank reconciliation, tax handling, and interactive UI, focusing instead on safe, attributable bookkeeping operations.

items.title: Cyera agrees to acquire Oasis Security for $1 billion to enhance AI agent security amid rising threats [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Cyera, a data security company valued at $12 billion, has signed a letter of intent to acquire Oasis Security for approximately $1 billion, mostly in cash with some shares. Oasis specializes in securing non-human identities, primarily AI agents, addressing the growing need for cybersecurity as AI agents proliferate in enterprises. Founded in 2022 and backed by investors including Accel and Cyberstarts, Oasis has raised about $195 million. Cyera plans to integrate Oasis's technology into its unified identity and data security platform, expanding its capabilities amid a surge in AI-related cybersecurity threats. This acquisition follows Cyera's recent purchases of Ryft and Genie Security and comes as the company surpasses $150 million in annual recurring revenue but remains unprofitable.

items.title: Cursor and Together AI deploy real-time, low-latency AI inference on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs for coding platform at scale [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Cursor, an AI-powered coding platform, partnered with Together AI to deliver real-time, low-latency inference within the editor feedback loop using NVIDIA Blackwell GB200 NVL72 GPUs. This collaboration optimized the inference stack end-to-end to meet strict latency requirements essential for live coding assistance, including debugging and refactoring as developers type. Together AI helped Cursor deploy production workloads early on NVIDIA Blackwell hardware, porting the inference stack to ARM-based hosts and developing custom kernels to leverage new Tensor Core instructions. They also established a repeatable pipeline for quantizing new model weights with NVIDIA TensorRT LLM and NVFP4, enabling rapid testing and deployment while preserving output quality. Cursor's production deployment runs across multiple data centers, supporting continuous model iteration and low-latency inference at scale.

items.title: AgentHound launches open-source offensive security framework for AI agent infrastructure with full-stack attack surface and Neo4j graph analysis [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: AgentHound is an open-source offensive security framework designed to assess AI agent infrastructure by performing reconnaissance, fingerprinting, credential looting, model inversion, and active exploitation across multiple layers including MCP, A2A, model gateways, inference servers, vector stores, MLOps, notebooks, and agent clients. It consolidates findings into a Neo4j graph to map attack paths, providing comprehensive visibility into vulnerabilities within the agentic stack. The framework includes capabilities such as credential inventory, modelfile and system-prompt enumeration, statistical model inversion to extract training data residues, and active exploitation techniques like tool poisoning and configuration implants. It supports cross-protocol attack path analysis, prompt injection modeling, and integrates detection rules aligned with OWASP MCP, Agentic Top 10, and MITRE ATLAS standards. AgentHound operates via a static collector binary with no external dependencies and offers lifecycle commands for scanning, looting, poisoning, and reverting changes, targeting authorized use cases only.

He emphasized that Modal's platform and isolation mechanisms themselves were not compromised in the incident.

Anatomy of a Frontier Lab Agent Intrusion: A Technical Timeline of the July 2026 Incident [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Anatomy of a Frontier Lab Agent Intrusion: A Technical Timeline of the July 2026 Incident Hugging Face just released this extremely detailed technical description of OpenAI's recent accidental cyberattack against their infrastructure. This attack was very sophisticated, and the resulting document doubles as a crash-course in modern adversarial security approaches. We're still waiting for more details from OpenAI on how their agent broke out of its sandbox. The package proxy that it found a zero-day vulnerability in has now been confirmed as JFrog's Artifactor, and JFrog and OpenAI Collaboration on Zero-Day Security Findings from JFrog links to the Artifactory 7.161.15 release notes which list 8 separate CVEs credited to OpenAI staff members. Having broken out through the HTTP proxy, the agent started by establishing a base of operations for the rest of the attack: [...] the agent escaped its sandbox by exploiting a zero-day in the package registry cache proxy, one of its primary permitted network egress with internet, then abused a public code-evaluation external sandbox hosted on a third-party provider's infrastructure. It was able to run commands as root/admin on that external sandbox and used it as a control, staging, and egress base for the entire campaign: it acted as an external launchpad for the agent. (That "third-party provider" turned out to be Modal.) It then spent five days - from Thursday 8th to Monday 13th July - executing a classic attack pattern: establishing C2 (command and control), reconnaissance, escalating privileges, dumping configuration information, exfiltrating the target data, and cleaning up after itself. (The first Hugging Face post about the incident followed on Thursday 16th, and OpenAI's confession came on Tuesday 21st.) Along the way it used all kinds of neat tricks. At one point it found an unsafe Jinja2 template execution and used it to execute arbitrary code: {{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.exec( "import gzip,base64; exec(gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode('')))" ) }} It broke out of a container within Hugging Face, stole a Kubernetes service-account token, and used that to further explore the network. It monkey-patched the Python socket library to hard-code an IP address when "DNS got in the way": socket.getaddrinfo = lambda *a, **k: [(2, 1, 6, '', ('', 443))] It even fired up its own Tailscale network to help exfiltrate data! tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking \ --state=mem: --socket=/tmp/ts.sock \ --socks5-server=127.0.0.1:1055 \ --no-logs-no-support >/tmp/td 2>&1 & The Hugging Face team note that, while a human attacker could have discovered and used the same exploits, the key difference here was speed: Our learning from this type of attack is that machine-speed offense makes ordinary weaknesses more expensive for defenders. LLM agents bring a step increase in the number of paths an attacker can test, the speed at which failed paths can be replaced, and the volume of evidence defenders must interpret. What's clear to me from this is that the very best frontier models, unencumbered by additional guardrails, will find an exploit if there is one to be found. The entire software industry needs to up its security game. items.title: Cursor Customers Fight Price Hikes in Contract Talks
items.content_text: Cursor, the pioneering AI coding app, is growing pretty well ahead of SpaceX's planned $60 billion purchase. But the company, which provides access to different AI models for coding work, last year shifted to charging more customers based on usage rather than flat rate subscriptions, and the move is now causing some heated contract renewal discussions. That seems to be pushing some customers to shift to Claude Code and other AI coding apps. We talked with an executive at an IT consulting firm who said they paid Cursor around $200,000 for 800 licenses in the 12 months ending in May of this year. When the contract came up for renewal, Cursor tried to charge the IT firm around $1.5 million for essentially the same amount of AI usage, according to this person and documents viewed by The Information. The IT firm "played hard ball" and negotiated the new yearlong contract down to $250,000, the person said. Cursor's acceptance of that offer shows how it may not have the level of pricing power enjoyed by other AI firms, most obviously Anthropic, at least for now.

items.title: Anthropic says its Mythos model found vulnerabilities in cryptographic algorithms that secure the internet [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview found weaknesses in key cryptographic algorithms, including a better attack on HAWK, a post-quantum signature scheme that human experts had reviewed for more than two years. The model found it in just 60 hours at an API cost of about $100,000. The findings don't affect systems in use today, but they show how AI could challenge core assumptions behind internet security, Anthropic says. items.title: Anthropic's Claude Code Reigns Despite Rising Interest in Codex, Open-Source Models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic is facing growing competition and customer skepticism over the lofty prices of AI tools. But the dominance of its blockbuster Claude Code product is proving hard to shake. Companies moved en masse to Claude Code between the end of 2025 and the early months of 2026, in many cases eroding the positions of Microsoft's GitHub Copilot and AI coding tool provider Cursor. In recent months, costs for Anthropic's customers have surged with its shift to usage-based pricing, while rival OpenAI has built Codex into a more formidable competitor and open-source models from China have grown significantly more capable. Still, even as they look for ways to contain costs, many enterprises have chosen to stick with Claude Code.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Are Quietly Teaming Up in Washington [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI and Anthropic are arch enemies whose leaders can't stand each other. But the two foes have formed an unholy alliance in Washington in the interest of self-preservation. With the Trump administration set to finalize its framework for regulating and evaluating "frontier models" by August 1, the two leading AI developers are quietly lobbying D.C. on a shared agenda: making sure lagging competitors like Meta and SpaceXAI also have to comply with government reviews of their models, and raising alarms about Chinese open-source models. Their alignment isn't obvious at first glance. But our sources tell us Anthropic and OpenAI have pushed to expand the type of models that would require government review under the framework to include those from their competitors. (They've discussed how the government and industry can develop an evaluation to determine whether a model requires extended review, based on its capabilities in cybersecurity or other tasks that could present national security risks.) Some of those rivals have disagreed, preferring that the government focus on Anthropic and OpenAI's models, given that those models are considered to be the most capable (and thus potentially dangerous and in need of a review).

items.title: Chinese AI Startup Moonshot Seeks More Nvidia Blackwell Chips for Next Model [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Beijing-based startup Moonshot AI, flush from the breakout success of its recently released model, Kimi K3, is already discussing plans for Kimi K4, which would be significantly larger in size than K3, according to two people with knowledge of the matter. There's just one problem: To train that new model, Moonshot would need access to more of Nvidia's advanced AI chips, which U.S. rules dictate should not be available to Chinese firms. Despite those restrictions, Moonshot trained Kimi K3-the world's largest open-source model, with 2.8 trillion parameters-on Nvidia chips, including the most advanced Blackwell ones, according to three people with knowledge of the matter, confirming part of a statement in an X post by White House senior official Michael Kratsios. Moonshot is now seeking access to more Blackwell chips to prepare for the development of future-generation models such as K4, according to two of the people.

items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei doubles down on open-weight risk stance while insisting he never called for a ban [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is once again warning about the risks of open AI models while insisting he has never called for a ban. He argues that authoritarian states like China could overtake the US and that open models could be misused for biological or cyberattacks. Critics say he's mostly trying to protect his own business from cheaper competition. The article Anthropic CEO Amodei doubles down on open-weight risk stance while insisting he never called for a ban appeared first on The Decoder.
